# Drawer

Figma: [06e. Drawer](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-935) · Family: 06 Navigation · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-06-14

A side-anchored panel that slides in from the leading or trailing edge for navigation, filters, or contextual detail - without leaving the page. Reuses the SheetHeader, SheetFooter, and content library; left/right anchor across LTR + RTL.

### Drawer

Full-height side panel that slides in from the leading or trailing edge for navigation, filters or contextual detail while the page stays in context. Shares SheetHeader, SheetFooter (Row layout) and the content library with BottomSheet and Modal.

Level: organism · Contains: SheetHeader, SheetFooter, Sheet Content / Blank, Sheet Content / List, Sheet Content / Form, Sheet Content / Summary

Use when:
- Filters in back-office tables, tweaked while results update (trailing side, Form content, Apply/Reset footer)
- Record detail beside a list (trailing side, Summary content)
- Temporary navigation on tablet or deep hierarchies (leading side, List content, footer off)

Don't use when:
- A short list of actions: use Menu or ActionList
- A focused mobile task: use BottomSheet
- A centered confirm: use Modal or Dialog
- Persistent desktop navigation: use NavigationRail or AppSidebar (shadcn-style)

Accessibility: Modal drawer: role=dialog, focus trap, Esc and scrim close; persistent drawer: no trap, use a complementary or nav landmark. One drawer at a time.

| Property in Figma | Code name | Type | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| showHeader | `showHeader` | boolean |  | true |
| showFooter | `showFooter` | boolean |  | true |
| Content | `content` | instance swap | default Sheet Content / Blank | 2699:12 |
| Side | `side` | variant | left, right | left |
| Direction | `direction` | variant | LTR, RTL | LTR |

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

A Drawer is a full-height panel that slides in from a side edge and sits above the page, for tasks that benefit from staying in context - app navigation, filters, or contextual detail. Unlike a Modal it hugs an edge rather than centering, and it can be wider and taller.

### When to use

- Primary navigation on tablet/desktop - a leading-edge nav drawer of destinations.
- Filters, facets, or settings that the user tweaks while watching results update.
- Contextual detail or a cart that should stay anchored beside the main content.

### When not to use

- A short list of actions - use a Menu / ActionList, not a whole panel.
- A focused mobile task - use BottomSheet (06c); a centered confirm - use Modal (06d).

### Live preview

### Anatomy

A full-height panel pinned to one edge over a scrim - the same header / content / footer stack as its siblings.

- Scrim - dims the rest of the screen; clicking it dismisses (for modal drawers).
- Panel - full-height, flush with one edge; only the inner corners (toward the content) are rounded with Radius/24.
- Header (SheetHeader) - title + close; toggle with showHeader.
- Content slot - a full-height area that fills the panel and scrolls; defaults to the Blank “your content here” slot.
- Footer (SheetFooter · Row layout) - a horizontal Primary + Secondary + overflow (···) menu pinned to the bottom; toggle with showFooter, showSecondary, showOverflow.

> **Info:** Drawer shares the SheetHeader, SheetFooter, content library, and Blank slot with BottomSheet and Modal - three surfaces, one set of parts.

### Sides & anchor

Two anchors. Think in leading/trailing, not just left/right - the physical edge flips with direction.

Leading (left in LTR)

Navigation drawers. Slides from the start edge; rounds its trailing corners.

Trailing (right in LTR)

Filters, detail, and cart panels. Slides from the end edge; rounds its leading corners.

- In RTL the edges mirror: the leading drawer anchors to the right, the trailing drawer to the left.

### Content library

Drawer uses the same shared library and Blank slot. List suits navigation and menus; Form suits filters; Summary suits detail.

Blank / Custom

The default - an empty slot to fill or swap.

List

Navigation destinations and menus.

Form

Filter and facet controls.

Summary

Contextual detail and breakdowns.

### Composition & slots

Same composable model as the other overlays - toggle the chrome, swap the content.

### Chrome toggles

- showHeader - title + close. showFooter - the bottom action row (Primary + Secondary + ··· overflow); turn it off for a pure navigation drawer.

### Content slot

- Defaults to the Blank slot. Swap to List (nav), Form (filters), Summary (detail) - or any component of your own.

> **Info:** A navigation drawer = showFooter off + List content. A filter drawer = trailing side + Form content + a footer with Apply / Reset.

### Direction - LTR and RTL

A leading drawer anchors to the start edge - left in LTR, right in RTL - and its header and content mirror.

LTR - leading on the left

IBM Plex Sans; close on the trailing (right) edge of the panel.

RTL - leading on the right

Noto Sans Arabic; panel mirrors to the right edge, content right-aligns.

### Behavior & dismissal

The panel slides in from its anchored edge. Two modes decide whether it blocks the page.

- Modal drawer - over a scrim; blocks the background; dismiss by scrim-click, swipe toward the edge, close, or Esc. Use on mobile and for focused side tasks.
- Standard (persistent) drawer - no scrim; sits beside the content and both stay usable. Use on wide desktop layouts for navigation.
- One drawer at a time - never open two; never pair a drawer with another overlay.
- Full height with internal scroll - header and footer stay pinned while the content scrolls.
- Focus is trapped inside a modal drawer and returns to the trigger on close.

> **Info:** Choose by whether the user needs the background: if they’re comparing against the page (filters, nav), prefer a standard drawer on desktop; if they must finish first, use a modal drawer with a scrim.

### Code examples

### Flutter

```dart
// Modal drawer (filters), trailing edge
Scaffold.of(context).openEndDrawer();

Scaffold(
  endDrawer: SyntropyDrawer(
    side: DrawerSide.trailing,    // leading · trailing
    showHeader: true,
    showFooter: true,
    header: SheetHeader(title: 'Filters', showClose: true),
    content: const FilterForm(),  // swap any content; default is Blank
    footer: SheetFooter(
      primary: Button.primary('Apply', onPressed: _apply),
      secondary: Button.secondary('Reset', onPressed: _reset),
    ),
  ),
  body: ...,
);
```

### Usage - Do and Don’t

Do

Do use a leading drawer for app navigation - a list of destinations, no footer.

Don’t

Don’t open a whole drawer for a short list of actions - use a Menu / ActionList instead.

Do

Do use a trailing drawer for filters the user tweaks while watching the results update.

Don’t

Don’t stack a drawer over another overlay, or open two at once - one surface at a time.

### Notes from the maintainer

> **Info:** Default content is the Blank slot - every drawer is a fillable panel out of the box. Swap to List (nav), Form (filters), or your own component.

> **Warning:** Side is physical (left/right). The Content slot shares one default across all 4 variants (Figma limit) - it defaults to Blank, which is direction-neutral.

> **Warning:** The panel drop shadow is a raw rgba effect - add effect/shadow/* tokens later.
